erwartburg.name: Wartburg
erwartburg.slogan: The hilltop fortress where Luther gave Germany its Bible.
erwartburg.line: Luther translated the New Testament here in about ten weeks, between May 1521 and March 1522.

erkraemerbruecke.name: Krämerbrücke
erkraemerbruecke.slogan: A medieval bridge you can shop, eat and live on.
erkraemerbruecke.line: Its 32 houses form the longest rows of inhabited buildings on any bridge in Europe.

ergoethe.name: Goethe's House
ergoethe.slogan: Fifty years of Weimar's greatest mind, room by room.
ergoethe.line: Nothing should be treasured more highly than the value of the day.
ergoethe.by: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, Maxims and Reflections, 1833

erdom.name: Erfurt Cathedral
erdom.slogan: A cathedral on a hill, ruled by one very large bell.
erdom.line: Its Gloriosa bell, cast in 1497, weighs 11.45 tonnes.

erannaamalia.name: Duchess Anna Amalia Library
erannaamalia.slogan: A Rococo hall of books under Weimar's gilded light.
erannaamalia.line: A fire on 2 September 2004 destroyed about 50,000 volumes, 12,500 of them irreplaceable.
